parsed.explanation: The operative regime is legality without safety: no trans-specific criminal statute and same-sex conduct lawful since 1998, but documented recurring police predation of LGBTIQ people — a police register since 2016, a 2017 'proven' registry, lured meetings to enrol people and harvest contacts, extortion, forced HIV testing, arbitrary charges in 2022–23 raids, ill-treatment and sexual abuse by officers with no remedy, plus police inaction on forced marriages. Public support is suppressed, politicians and the senior religious authority are openly hostile, and no anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse exists. In-country gender-affirming care is absent, so a visitor's medication continuity fails. Border, document-marker and trans-custody questions are unresolved, not cleared. Dated social evidence (2013) is not treated as current, but 2024 police practice is. This sits below thinly-policed extortion states because the predation is documented, recurring, and unremedied.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No information on entry rules, visa practice, passport markers, airport screening or inspection-stage outing.
entry_documents.interaction: Unresolved rather than cleared; a document/presentation mismatch at a checkpoint would feed into the documented police registration and extortion practice, but the border stage itself is unsourced.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police register of LGBTIQ people (2016) and a 2017 government registry of 'proven' LGBT persons; 2024 documented luring into fake meetings to register, social-media contact harvesting and extortion (10+ cases in one province); arbitrary criminal charges in 2022/23 raids; ill-treatment and sexual abuse by officers.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: None documented; trans detention placement and conditions unsourced.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Registration mechanisms convert a stop, hotel record or app encounter into durable exposure and blackmail leverage, with no documented remedy.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National-level police facilities show documented ill-treatment, sexual abuse, forced HIV testing and extortion of LGBT detainees; no trans-specific placement or conditions record.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Unitary state, so national police practice is the operative facility regime a visitor would meet; whether registries are the same instrument and still operational is unsourced.

care_services.exposure: No gender-affirming services in-country; transition requires going abroad; most doctors lack expertise; LGBTQ patients report disrespectful treatment; some clinicians offer pseudo-scientific 'cure methods'. A visitor's HRT continuity has no reliable domestic route.
care_services.protection: An NGO-drafted HRT protocol used to educate endocrinologists; a regional study includes guidance for trans migrants but its country findings are not set out.
care_services.interaction: Emergency or lost-medication need exposes the visitor to staff who are documented as disrespectful, with no regulator or complaint route recorded.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No SOGI anti-discrimination protection (2022 statute retains only 'sex'); public support effectively suppressed; politicians' homophobic/transphobic remarks part of everyday politics; senior religious authority condemns same-sex relations and anti-discrimination laws.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: None documented; activists have no access to the health ministry or other authorities, so no institutional counterweight.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State and religious framing of LGBTIQ people as a moral problem licenses the documented police extortion and public hostility, raising severity after any outing.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. No findings on LGBTQ minors, schools or a trans adult travelling with a minor.
minors_guardians.interaction: Unresolved; no basis in the dossier to assess a guardian-minor pairing at borders, facilities or care settings.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 2024 police extortion and blackmail of LGBT people; police inaction on forced/sham marriages imposed on LGBT people; 2013 account of physical and psychological abuse, including by police, after disclosure (dated).
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented; no hate-crime provision and no recorded prosecution of attackers or abusive officers.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Where police are themselves extortionists and documented as declining to intervene, a visitor has no realistic route to protection after assault or blackmail.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination statute covering SOGI, no relationship recognition, no documented court relief for LGBT victims, NGOs forced to operate anonymously with no ministry access; whether registries remain operational is unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: None documented as operating; the only positive items (decriminalisation since 1998, age of consent 16) create no recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of remedy means each documented police harm recurs without correction, and unresolved border/registry questions cannot be resolved in-country.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in kind: police stop and interrogate, confiscate documents, extort and fine, with courts deferring to police. This dossier is somewhat worse — a formal LGBTIQ register, documented sexual abuse and contact harvesting, openly hostile political and religious framing, and no care route — but shares the absence of a trans-specific criminal statute or credible lethal pathway, so it sits just below that anchor rather than far below.

Close: transport police extorting trans travellers, confiscating documents, overnight cells with harassment, oversight dismissing complaints, occasional clinic-won compensation. This dossier has comparable extortion and registration machinery but no documented working legal clinic or compensation, plus openly hostile state framing and absent care; roughly comparable, marginally below.

Materially safer than this dossier: trained border officers, written reasons, access to counsel, compensation for unlawful holding and a functioning tribunal. Here nothing analogous is documented — no border practice, no counsel access, no relief, and police are the documented harm-doers rather than a remedy.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is one of formal legality with an actively hostile and predatory enforcement layer. Same-sex conduct is lawful and there is no trans-specific criminal offence, which keeps this out of the severe band, but police maintain LGBTIQ registers, lure people to enrolment meetings, harvest contacts and extort, conducted raids with forced testing and arbitrary charges, and are documented committing ill-treatment and sexual abuse without any remedy. No anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse, no relationship recognition, and no in-country gender-affirming care mean a visitor who is outed carries exposure at the police, health and street levels at once. Border and custody-stage trans specifics are unresolved, not cleared, and are not credited as safety.
